title: RevokeAccessFlow
wrapsNative: sheet(isPresented:content:) with interactiveDismissDisabled holding the item, Date.RelativeFormatStyle, MonarchConsequenceList, MonarchTypeToConfirmInput, MonarchInlineNotice and MonarchButtons; a second sheet with MonarchStepUpAuthDialog when re-authentication is required
summary: A recipe, not a component: confirm revoking an API key, an OAuth client, portal access, sessions or devices, listing what is revoked, when it was last used and what happens, with optional type-to-confirm and re-authentication.
whenToUse: Behind every Revoke, Sign out or Remove action on keys, connected apps, sessions, devices or someone's portal access.
whenNotToUse: For a device list with its own simple confirmation, MonarchDeviceList's built-in alert is enough. For leaving a workspace yourself, use the leave workspace recipe.
api: MonarchButton("Revoke key", variant: .danger, isLoading: isRevoking, fullWidth: true) { … }
MonarchStepUpAuthDialog(description: "Revoking access needs you to confirm it’s you.", onVerified: revoke, onVerify: { credential in … })

states.name: confirm
states.description: The question naming what is revoked, a line on what it means, the item with its prefix and last-used time, the consequences, and a danger button naming the action.

states.name: type to confirm
states.description: For keys and OAuth clients, the danger button stays disabled until the name is typed exactly.

states.name: step-up
states.description: When re-authentication is required, the danger button opens MonarchStepUpAuthDialog; the revocation runs after it verifies.

states.name: revoking
states.description: The danger button shows its spinner; Cancel is disabled and the sheet cannot be swiped away.

states.name: failed
states.description: A danger MonarchInlineNotice in the sheet; the person can try again.

appearance: Every part is an existing Monarch component in the theme: the heading style title, the code style for the key prefix, MonarchConsequenceList, MonarchTypeToConfirmInput and danger and ghost MonarchButtons.
platformNotes: The web's RevokeAccessFlow is one component with built-in copy for five kinds (api-key, oauth-client, portal-access, session, device) and plural forms. On iOS it is a recipe: the copy is the app's, written for its kind and count, and the step is a sheet because a system alert cannot hold a list, a text field with a match check, or a pending state. Danger is the default for keys and OAuth clients (they cannot be undone); for sessions, devices and portal access, which can sign in again, use a plain confirmation alert or the same sheet with warning wording. The web's stepUp prop is the second sheet with MonarchStepUpAuthDialog. Android composes the same recipe.
accessibility: The title has the header trait; the item is one element read as its name, prefix and last-used time.
MonarchConsequenceList reads each consequence with its kind.
MonarchTypeToConfirmInput announces when the typed name matches.
The row's Revoke button is named with the item ("Revoke CI deploy key").
Buttons are MonarchButtons with 44-point touch targets and a busy state while revoking; the sheet cannot be dismissed while revoking.
edgeCases: For several items, list each one and put the count in the title and the button ("Revoke 3 keys").
An item never used reads "Never used" instead of a time.
Reset the typed phrase each time the sheet opens.
